title: NOPTIS Studio
descGiDInspector: NOPTIS Studio is a small application that instantly breaks a NOPTIS GID apart and presents all information contained in the identifier.
gidPlaceholder: What is this GID number used for?
prefixDesc:
Purpose: The PREFIX is the first 4 digits of a key-based NOPTIS GID.

It identifies what type of object the GID represents, for example a line, stop, vehicle, journey, block, zone or deviation case.

This segment is needed so a system can understand the object category before interpreting the rest of the number. Without the prefix, the same numeric value could mean different things depending on context.

9011 = Line
9015 = Service Journey
9021 = Stop Area
9022 = Stop Point
9031 = Vehicle
9041 = Block
9076 = Deviation Case
9081 = Zone

Typical use: Route the parsing logic. If the prefix is 9011, the remaining segments should be interpreted as a line GID. If the prefix is 9022, the remaining segments should be interpreted as a stop point GID.
thmNumberDesc:
Purpose: The TPA segment is the 3-digit Transport Authority number.

It identifies the Transport Authority that owns or defines the number space for the object.

This segment is needed because NOPTIS is designed for environments with multiple transport authorities. The same line number, stop number or TPO number may exist in different authority contexts.

TPA = Transport Authority
TPA number = Transport Authority number
Example role: the authority responsible for the public transport network

Typical use: Determine which authority's number space the object belongs to, avoid number collisions between authorities, and interpret the rest of the GID in the correct authority context.
contractorNumberDesc:
Purpose: The TPO segment is the Transport Operator number.

It identifies the operator that performs traffic within the number space of a specific Transport Authority.

This segment is used for objects that are operator-specific, such as vehicles, blocks, duties, employees and dead runs.

It is needed because many operational objects are not only linked to a Transport Authority, but also to the Transport Operator that operates or manages them.

TPA = Transport Authority
TPO = Transport Operator
TPO number = the operator's number within the TPA context

Example: Vehicle 12345 under one TPO is not necessarily the same vehicle as vehicle 12345 under another TPO.

Typical use: Identify which Transport Operator a vehicle, block, duty, employee or dead run belongs to.
paddingDesc:
Purpose: The ZEROS segment is padding.

It means that this part of the 16-digit GID structure is not used for the current object type.

Padding is needed because key-based NOPTIS GIDs use a fixed-length structure, even when an object type does not need every available segment.

Example:
A Line GID may use the line number segment,
while the remaining unused digits are filled with zeroes.

Typical use: Validate that unused parts of a key-based GID are correctly filled. If a segment is defined as padding, it should normally contain only zeroes.
lineNumberDesc:
Purpose: The LINE segment is the internal numeric line number.

It identifies the line within the Transport Authority's number space.

This is not always the same as the public line designation shown to passengers. The public designation can contain letters or formatting, while the GID segment must be numeric.

Public display: 5, 7A, X1 or Express Line
GID segment: numeric line identifier used by the system

Typical use: Connect a GID to a line object, group journeys by line, interpret direction and journey data, or show technical/debug information about which line an object belongs to.
journeyDeadRunDesc:
Purpose: The JOURNEY segment identifies a service journey or a dead run, depending on the GID prefix.

A service journey is a passenger-carrying planned journey. A dead run is a non-public vehicle movement, for example a vehicle moving to or from a depot, garage or start position.

This segment is needed because a line alone is not enough to identify a specific run. A line can have many journeys during an operating day.

Line = traffic product or route family
Service Journey = passenger-carrying planned run
Dead Run = non-public vehicle movement

Typical use: Match real-time reports to the correct planned journey, debug vehicle assignment, connect operational events to the timetable, or identify the exact journey a vehicle is operating.
stopNumberDesc:
Purpose: The STOP segment normally identifies the Stop Area number.

A Stop Area is the stop as a whole, such as a station, terminal or stop area containing one or more individual stop points.

Stop Area: Central Station
Stop Points: platform 1, platform 2, quay A, quay B

This segment is needed because passenger information often needs to refer either to the whole stop area or to a specific stop point inside it.

Typical use: Configure departure boards at stop-area level, fetch all stop points inside a stop area, group departures by station or terminal, or apply messages to a whole stop area.
localPositionNumberDesc:
Purpose: The LOCAL_POS segment identifies the local Stop Point number inside a Stop Area.

A Stop Point is the exact place where passengers board or alight, such as a platform, track, gate, quay or bus position.

This segment is needed because one Stop Area can contain several Stop Points. The Stop Area identifies the general location, while the local position identifies the exact boarding or alighting point.

Stop Area: Central Station
Local positions: platform 1, platform 2, quay A, quay B

Typical use: Identify the correct platform, track, quay or stop position for a departure, distinguish a whole stop from a specific stop point, and handle real-time stop point changes.
localEntranceNumberDesc:
Purpose: The ENTRANCE segment identifies the local Station Entrance Point number inside a Stop Area.

A Station Entrance Point is a point where a passenger can enter or leave a station.

This segment is needed because larger stations can have multiple entrances and exits. These can matter for walking routes, accessibility, transfer planning and disruption information.

Stop Area: Central Station
Entrances: north entrance, south entrance, main hall, platform tunnel

Typical use: Describe which entrance is available or closed, connect entrances to stop points, support transfer links, or guide passengers through a station.
nodeNumberDesc:
Purpose: The NODE segment corresponds to the Journey Pattern Point number.

A Journey Pattern Point is a general point used in a journey pattern. It can be a Stop Point, Via Point, Parking Point or another point used for route and timing logic.

This segment is needed because not every point in a route is a passenger stop. Some points are used for routing, timing, mapping, vehicle positioning or parking.

Stop Point = passengers can board or alight
Via Point = clarifies the route path
Parking Point = vehicle can wait or park
Timing Point = supports progress and prediction logic

Typical use: Let AVL systems, journey patterns, route links and progress reports refer to where a vehicle is, where an event occurred, or how a route is structured.
vehicleNumberDesc:
Purpose: The VEHICLE segment identifies the vehicle number within a TPO context.

A vehicle GID combines the object type, the TPA number, the TPO number and the vehicle number.

This is needed because vehicle numbers are often assigned by the Transport Operator, not globally across all Transport Authorities and operators.

TPA + TPO + Vehicle number = unique vehicle context

TPO A / Vehicle 12345
TPO B / Vehicle 12345

These are different vehicles.

Typical use: Identify which physical vehicle is operating a journey, connect APC data to a vehicle, troubleshoot AVL reports, and track vehicle assignments.
blockNumberDesc:
Purpose: The BLOCK segment identifies the block number within a TPO context.

A block is a planned piece of vehicle work. It can contain a sequence of journeys and tasks intended to be operated by the same vehicle.

This segment is needed because traffic operations often manage vehicle work by blocks rather than only by individual journeys.

Block = vehicle work package
Journey 1 + Journey 2 + Journey 3 = one block

A vehicle may sign on to a block, and that block can contain several journeys.

Typical use: Vehicle scheduling, block sign-on, operational control, and understanding which journeys belong together during an operating day.
dutyNumberDesc:
Purpose: The DUTY segment identifies the duty number within a TPO context.

A duty is normally related to staff work rather than vehicle work. It represents a planned work assignment, often for a driver.

This segment is needed because staff scheduling and vehicle scheduling are connected, but not identical.

Vehicle block = what the vehicle should do
Driver duty = what the driver should do

A duty can cover one or more vehicle tasks, and a vehicle block can be worked by one or more duties depending on the operation.

Typical use: Driver sign-on and sign-off, staff assignment, operational follow-up, and linking staff work to vehicle journeys.
employeeNumberDesc:
Purpose: The EMPLOYEE segment identifies the employee number within a TPO context.

It is typically used for drivers or other operational staff.

This segment is needed because employee numbers are usually internal to the Transport Operator. The same employee number may exist under another TPO.

TPO A / Employee 12345
TPO B / Employee 12345

These are different employees.

Typical use: Driver identification, sign-on, audit trails, operational control, and historical analysis.
caseNumberDesc:
Purpose: The CASE segment identifies a deviation case number.

A deviation case is a container for information about a disturbance, deviation or operational change. It can include a reason, passenger or staff messages, publication scope and operational actions.

This segment is needed because a disturbance or traffic change needs a stable identity. The same case may create messages, control actions and updates in several systems.

Deviation Case = the container
Message = information shown to passengers or staff
Control Action = change applied to the production plan

Typical use: Track a disturbance from creation to publication, connect submitted changes with real-time output, group related messages, or revoke and update an operational action.
zoneTypeDesc:
Purpose: The ZONE_TYPE segment identifies what kind of zone the GID refers to.

A zone can represent different concepts, such as a tariff zone, traffic analysis zone, administrative zone, technical zone, parking area or another geographical grouping.

This segment is needed because the same zone number may only be meaningful together with its zone type.

Zone type: tariff
Zone number: 123

Zone type: technical area
Zone number: 123

These do not have to represent the same zone.

Typical use: Separate fare logic from traffic analysis, information regions, parking areas or technical coverage areas.
zoneNumberDesc:
Purpose: The ZONE_NO segment identifies the actual zone number within the selected zone type.

The zone type explains what kind of zone it is. The zone number identifies the specific zone inside that type.

This segment is needed so a system can refer to one specific geographical, fare-related, administrative or technical area.

Zone type + Zone number = specific zone identity

Typical use: Connect stops or journey pattern points to tariff zones, information regions, parking areas or other spatial groupings.
placeNumberDesc:
Purpose: The PLACE segment identifies the place number.

A Place is a named geographical object that can be used to define the origin or destination of a passenger trip.

This segment is needed because destination texts, journey planning and passenger-facing information often need to refer to named places, not only stops.

Place = named geographical location
Stop Area = public transport stop or station
Destination Display = passenger-facing destination text

Typical use: Destination displays, origin and destination search, passenger-facing naming, and relations between named places and nearby stop areas.
equipmentNumberDesc:
Purpose: The EQUIP segment identifies an infrastructure or equipment-related object number in this segment model.

In the NOPTIS GID context, this may correspond to an object such as a bridging device. A bridging device can be an elevator, escalator, stairway or similar object used to pass an obstacle in a transfer link.

The label EQUIP should therefore be understood as an application-friendly segment name for an infrastructure/equipment-related object.

Possible object type:
Bridging Device

Examples:
elevator, escalator, stairway, passage device

This segment is needed because infrastructure and equipment objects may need stable identities, especially when they can be opened, closed, monitored or shown in passenger information.

Typical use: Accessibility information, elevator or escalator disruptions, transfer planning, station infrastructure and technical status messages.
virtualVehicleNumberDesc:
Purpose: The VIRTUAL_VEHICLE_NO segment identifies a virtual vehicle number.

A virtual vehicle is a temporary or fallback vehicle identity used when the actual vehicle number is not available.

This segment is needed because real-time systems may know that a vehicle exists and is reporting data, even before the real vehicle identity is known.

Actual vehicle known:
Use Vehicle GID

Actual vehicle unknown:
Use Virtual Vehicle GID as fallback

Typical use: Fallback identity in AVL and real-time flows, especially during incomplete assignment, missing vehicle master data or temporary tracking scenarios.
